title: Unified Inference: Q2 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Sofia Patel
summary: Comprehensive product document combining product overview, PRD, design specs, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference (Q2 2026).
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements & acceptance criteria), high-level design specs, roadmap & themes for the next two quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product area (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments). It is intended for product, engineering, go-to-market, and customer success stakeholders.

Goals (Q2 2026)

- Ship a hardened Unified Inference v1.3 that provides a single API surface across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with predictable performance and rollout controls.
- Reduce customer token cost by 12% (measured median per-token cost across sampled workloads) via caching/batching and model selection recommendations.
- Improve 99th percentile request latency by 20% for short-chat workloads (<= 256 tokens).
- Provide clear pricing tiers and packaging options for SMB, Mid-market, and Enterprise customers.

Scope

In-scope: hosted API improvements (streaming, function calling), Dedicated capacity controls (reserved + burst), Private deployment packaging (VPC + on-prem installer), Redwood Console enhancements (route/model dashboards), Redwood Optimize recommendations integration.
Out-of-scope: core research on new model architectures, third-party marketplace integrations (deferred to Q4).

Product Requirements (PRD)

1) Functional requirements
- FR-01: Single API endpoints for text-generation and chat that support function/tool-calling and structured output (JSON schema enforcement).
- FR-02: Streaming responses with token-level deltas and the ability to attach per-token latency metadata.
- FR-03: Model routing policy config that supports priority tiers (latency-first, cost-first, region-affinity) and automatic fallback to quantized variants.
- FR-04: Per-route KV/prefix caching controls with TTL and cache-visibility metrics surfaced in Console.
- FR-05: Dedicated capacity autoscaling policies with guaranteed baseline throughput and optional burst buckets.
- FR-06: Private deployment bundle (VPC control plane + on-prem agent) with KMS integration (customer-managed keys).

2) Non-functional requirements
- NFR-01 (Reliability): 99.9% availability for hosted inference endpoints for paid customers (SLA target, measured monthly).
- NFR-02 (Latency): 99th percentile tail latency <= 250ms for short-chat (<= 128 tokens) under nominal load for Hosted API (region US-WEST-2).
- NFR-03 (Security): Audit logging enabled for all Private deployments; logs retained per customer retention policy (default 90 days).
- NFR-04 (Scalability): Dedicated pools must scale to support 50k concurrent token streams per pool type.

3) Acceptance criteria (examples)
- AC-01: Run the perf-suite against v1.3 and demonstrate 20% 99p latency improvement on short-chat compared to v1.1 baseline.
- AC-02: Billing validation test that exercises caching to ensure cost reduction metrics are reflected on token invoicing.
- AC-03: Security review sign-off for KMS integration and audit log storage.

Design Specs (high-level)

Architecture summary
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine with continuous batching and KV cache management.
- Control plane: centralized routing and policy engine (Policy API) with per-customer config.
- Observability: per-token tracing (span per generate call), route/model dashboards in Redwood Console.

Design details
- Model catalog: each model entry contains model_id, quantization_profiles (q4_0, q8_0), latency_profile_{p50,p95,p99}, and compatible_fallbacks. These are surfaced via Catalog API (GET /v1/catalog).
- Routing policy: JSON mesh where teams can declare policies like: {"priority":"latency","preferred_models":["redwood-llama-70b-q8"],"fallbacks":["redwood-llama-70b-q4"]}. The Policy API supports evaluation against prioritized constraints.
- Cache design: LRU prefix cache per tenant shard, configurable max_entries and TTL. Cache hit metrics exported to Prometheus: redwood.cache.hits, redwood.cache.misses, redwood.cache.evictions.

Operational considerations
- Autoscaling: Dedicated pool autoscaler uses signal from request queue depth and per-GPU utilization. Scale-up threshold: request_queue_depth > 200 for 30s. Scale-down cooldown: 5m.
- Rollouts: support canary (5% traffic), A/B (50/50), and instant rollback via model pinning.

Roadmap & Themes (Q2 2026–2027)

Themes
- Theme A: Performance & Cost Optimization — lower per-token unit economics and faster tails.
- Theme B: Enterprise Readiness — SLA, KMS, audit logging, private packaging.
- Theme C: Developer Experience — clearer SDKs, streaming ergonomics, and Console per-route controls.

Quarter milestones
- 2026-Q2 (Apr–Jun): Unified Inference v1.3 release candidate, public pricing tiers published, Dedicated autoscaling GA, basic Private VPC package beta.
- 2026-Q3 (Jul–Sep): Private on-prem installer GA, Redwood Console model-level tracing, Optimize recommendations v2 with per-route quantization suggestions.

Pricing & Packaging Notes

Pricing principles
- Transparent unit economics: publish per-token and per-embedding base rates with examples for typical workloads.
- Predictable committed pricing: reserved Dedicated capacity discounts (monthly/annual).
- Clear enterprise add-ons: extended retention, compliance packages, premium SLA/Support.

Suggested pricing tiers (example guidance)
- Hosted (self-serve):
  - Developer: $0.0006 / prompt-token + $0.0008 / completion-token (suitable for prototyping).
  - Growth: $0.00045 / prompt-token + $0.0006 / completion-token (volume discounts kick in at $5k/mo).
  - Enterprise: Custom pricing with SLAs and 24/7 support.
- Embeddings: $0.00005 / vector (128-d baseline).
- Dedicated: Reserve GPU pool starting at $10k/mo for small pools (16 A100-equivalent vCPU units), scaling to $120k+/mo for large reserved clusters.
- Private: Platform license + deployment fee; typical first-year TCV starts at $150k (including 1-year support & installation).

Packaging options
- Self-serve Hosted API (credit card onboarding).
- Dedicated Monthly/Annual (contract + commitment).
- Private VPC (managed control plane) and Private On-Prem (air-gapped installer) — both require an enterprise contract.

Billing considerations
- Cache and reuse: bill based on effective consumed tokens after cache hits and prefix reuse; ensure billing pipeline receives cache_hit_ratio metric to compute invoiced tokens.
- Reserved capacity: committed discounts applied against consumed tokens up to reserved throughput; overage computed at mid-tier rates.

Release Notes: Unified Inference v1.3 (2026-05-02)

Highlights
- Single API surface for chat & generation with function calling GA.
- Streaming with token-level metadata and lower startup latency for short-chat workloads (meets 20% 99p improvement vs v1.1).
- Dedicated autoscaling GA with baseline throughput guarantees and burst buckets.
- Private VPC beta with KMS integration and audit logging enabled.
- Redwood Console: per-route cost and latency breakdowns; cache visibility metrics.

Behavioral changes
- Model fallback behavior: when routing policy triggers fallback to a quantized variant, output tokens may have minor qualitative differences; teams should validate with evals (see Quality Guardrails doc).
- Billing: effective billed tokens will reflect cache hits; customers may see lower invoice totals after caching is enabled.

Known issues & mitigations
- Issue: Rare 5xx when scaling under extreme burst > 3x baseline. Mitigation: Autoscaler cooldown tuned; temporary soft-fallback to lower-cost model variants during extreme bursts. Runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/traffic-spike-autoscale.
- Issue: KMS permissions edge-case in Azure regions causing onboarding delays; Mitigation: updated installer checks and documented workaround in onprem-packaging.

Rollout & Phased deployment
- Week 0: Release candidate builds deployed to staging; internal smoke tests and perf-suite run.
- Week 1: Canary to 5% of traffic (low-risk customers), collect metrics for 72 hours.
- Week 2–3: Incremental ramp to 50% with anomaly detection; engage account owners for Enterprise customers.
- Week 4: Full rollout pending sign-off from SRE, Security, and Product.

- Infrastructure/SRE: Ethan Brooks (eng-sre) — autoscaling and rollout.
- Security: Amina Khatri (security-and-compliance) — KMS and audit logging review.

Success metrics (KPIs)
- Latency: 99p short-chat latency (target <= 250ms).
- Cost: Median per-token cost reduction >= 12% for customers adopting recommendations.
- Adoption: 25% of active paid customers use Dedicated or Private packaging within 6 months of GA.
- Reliability: Monthly availability >= 99.9% for paid endpoints.

Action items & next steps
1. Engineering: finalize Policy API schema and start integration (owner: Liam Chen) — due 2026-04-30.
2. Product: publish official pricing page and example calculators (owner: Sofia Patel) — due 2026-05-10.
3. GTM: prepare launch materials and enterprise playbook for Dedicated/Private options (owner: GTM) — due 2026-05-20.
4. SRE: run game-day for autoscaler under 5x burst (owner: Ethan Brooks) — scheduled 2026-05-05.
